entities.name: PMID:10752939
observations: Primary human conjunctival fibroblast monolayers increased peripheral-blood eosinophil viability by 35.9% at day 4 and 12.8% at day 8 versus medium alone; GM-CSF, IL-3, and IL-5 neutralization partially reduced the effect.
After 4 days of direct coculture, LPS induced greater eosinophil peroxidase release than in freshly isolated eosinophils (P=0.01); coculture supported eosinophil adherence.
Conjunctival fibroblast-conditioned medium did not enhance eosinophil survival under the tested conditions, indicating that direct contact or a short-range signal may be required.

entities.name: PMID:12036989
observations: In inflamed juvenile conjunctival nevus, lesional fibroblasts enhanced eosinophil adherence and both lesional and extralesional fibroblasts increased eosinophil peroxidase release, but fibroblasts did not increase eosinophil viability; effects were context dependent.

entities.name: Conjunctival fibroblasts
observations: Primary human conjunctival fibroblasts can support peripheral-blood eosinophil survival and enhance stimulated secretory responsiveness in direct coculture; conditioned medium alone was ineffective for survival in one study.

entities.name: Peripheral-blood eosinophils
observations: Human peripheral-blood eosinophils show increased viability, adherence, and LPS-triggered eosinophil peroxidase release after direct coculture with some primary conjunctival fibroblast preparations.
